whatThisRowDoesNotDischarge: I read the form. Request page 4 is headed REQUEST TO SEAL CRIMINAL RECORDS and prints, in a ruled box directly under that heading: "If you are only requesting to expunge cases, check the 'No' box in Section 12, skip to the bottom of the form and sign it." Section 12 then reads "I am requesting to seal records.  [ ] Yes   [ ] No (If no, skip Sections 13 - 23.)", and Section 13 is the sealing case table -- the fields these builders name with the "4 - " prefix. The "section 4" of FIX94's question is that table. In the AcroForm, "12 - Seal Records" is a SINGLE field carrying TWO widgets: a /Yes widget at x=81.0 and a /No widget at x=162.0. "No" is therefore electronically expressible, but pdf-lib's check() only ever sets a field to its on-value (/Yes), so on an expungement route the No box is unreachable and both boxes stay Off. WHAT THE DELIVERED PAGE SHOWS, rastered at 307 dpi and 384 dpi and looked at: Section 12 has NEITHER box ticked, and row 1 of the Section 13 sealing table is fully populated with the participant's case number, arresting agency, charge, arrest date and outcome. WHAT THE FORM REQUIRES OF THIS ROUTE: on its face, an expunge-only petitioner answers Section 12 "No" and skips Sections 13-23, which would leave the Section 13 table blank and the No box ticked. On that reading VF01's finding against il-exp-qualprob-set -- "the inactive sealing table is populated" -- reads correctly, and the mirrored treatment in il-seal-2yr-set and il-seal-3yr-set is the consistent one. WHAT REMAINS A JUDGEMENT, AND IS NOT MINE TO SETTLE: the form is a combined Request to Expunge AND/OR Seal, so a petitioner may genuinely be asking to expunge some cases and seal others on one Request, in which case Section 12 is "Yes" and a populated Section 13 row is right -- but then the route identity, the route summary and the participant instructions would have to say so, and here they do not. I am not deciding which remedy this route asks for. I am reporting that the state now delivered -- Section 12 unanswered while Section 13 is populated -- is not a state the form's printed instruction contemplates on any reading, and that this is a legal-design question for whoever holds the route, not a rendering bug I should have quietly picked a side on.

REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING is declared, not discharged. 113 refusals are named as facts the participant still owes, and participant-instructions.md prints the controlling record's requiredBeforeFiling steps in the record's own words. Naming an owed fact is not obtaining it.

The 'I am completing this form for myself' checkbox is ticked by the builder as participant.self_represented. That is a participant assertion the platform is making on the fixture's behalf. It is declared, and it is consistent with a self-represented fixture, but it is a participant election and a reader should see it as one. No signature, notarization, consent, clerk act, fee or judicial finding was fabricated anywhere in this packet.
The route summary's expunge-versus-seal election is left to the participant, and this row does not decide it.

openQuestionThisLaneDidNotDecide.where: CR-65 pages 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8 -- fields Text1, Text4, Text5, Text7 and Court Case Number, Court Case Number_2, Court Case Number_4
openQuestionThisLaneDidNotDecide.observed: Each of those pages carries a caption box printed 'Court Case Number' with the sublabel '(Assigned by Clerk)'. The packet prefills all of them with the participant's underlying criminal case number. CR-65 page 7 carries the same box and this packet leaves it blank, because page 7 is blanket-protected -- so the packet is already inconsistent with itself about who owns that box. The form separately provides an explicit line 'COURT CASE NUMBER TO BE EXPUNGED:' for the underlying case, which is written and correct.
openQuestionThisLaneDidNotDecide.whyThisLaneDidNotChangeIt: Deciding it means deciding whether that caption box is the expungement petition's own number, which a clerk assigns at filing and which the participant cannot know, or the underlying criminal case number. data/record-clearing/legal-design-intake/AL.memo.json establishes neither -- it contains no rule about the caption, the case number, or clerk assignment -- and this lane will not author a legal conclusion the held record does not carry, in either direction. Removing seven writes on a reading I cannot source would be as much an invention as leaving them.
openQuestionThisLaneDidNotDecide.whatIsNeededToDecideIt: One line in the Alabama legal-design record, or counsel, saying which number belongs in the CR-65 caption box. If it is the clerk's, seven writes per family become required-before-filing blanks. This is reported so it cannot disappear, not repaired.

provenFromTheSavedBytes.method: Not from the builder's field map. For each delivered PDF: every page's content streams were decompressed; each was hashed and excluded if it matched a content stream of one of the two source PDFs; the remaining builder-added streams were tokenized, their `Do` calls followed into the flattened widget XObjects, and every show-text operator decoded with the text and graphics matrices preceding it, carrying its device-space origin, font, size, render mode and fill colour.
provenFromTheSavedBytes.sourceStreamsPreservedMeans: On all 11 pages of both fixtures at least one content stream hashed identically to a stream of the official source, and the decoded builder-added ink accounts for the writes and nothing else. The official form's own ink was not rewritten.
provenFromTheSavedBytes.whyThatMatters: One decoded show-text operator per declared write, and no more, is the measurement that rules out source-authored default values: a default carried by the source form would have been flattened into ink too and would have decoded as an extra show with no declared write behind it. There were none, in either fixture, on any of the six families.
provenFromTheSavedBytes.pagesWithNoBuilderInkMeans: Packet page 7 is CR-65 page 7, the Certificate of Service, and packet page 11 is C-10-CRIMINAL page 3, the judge's order. Neither carries a single byte of builder ink in either fixture. No certificate of mailing is completed before the mailing, no server signature, no service date or method, no judicial finding and no clerk act is fabricated.
provenFromTheSavedBytes.invisibleWriteTest: Every decoded show was checked for text render mode 3 or 7, for a white fill, and for a zero or negative effective size. None was found.
provenFromTheSavedBytes.unexpectedValueTest: Every decoded string was matched against the closed set of values the fixture holds. Nothing else appears in the ink.

determinismTwoRuns.method: The builder was run, the whole family directory copied aside, the builder run again, and the two trees compared with diff -r. No file differed. This was done at each of the three stages: on the untouched FIX09-repaired machinery, after the fit-or-refuse repair, and after the Social Security repair.
determinismTwoRuns.note: The builder stamps a fixed date, 2026-09-03T00:00:00.000Z, into every PDF's creation and modification date rather than a wall clock, which is why these digests are stable under a hash-bound receipt.

nineCounters.visualDefectsProvenance: The verifier prints visualDefects 0, and on its own that number is worthless here: it printed 0 while the boundary packet was rendering a clipped, semantically wrong case number on the Social Security line. The 0 recorded above is this lane's own measurement, not the verifier's -- every show-text operator in both fixtures measured against its own clip box for overflow, against render mode and fill for invisibility, and the decisive pages read off 200 dpi pdftoppm rasters. It is still a builder's measurement of its own output and it decides nothing.
nineCounters.whatTheseCountersDoNotSee: The same blind spot FIX09 recorded, confirmed again here: all nine read zero on the faulted bytes and all nine read zero on the repaired bytes. They accept the field map as their classification authority, so they can ask whether a write happened but never whether it was true, and they cannot see ink cut off by a widget's clip path. Every defect that mattered in this row was found by decoding the saved bytes and by looking at rendered pages.
